summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia and allogeneic cord blood transplant complicated by chronic graft-versus-host disease, was admitted with nausea, brown emesis, and fever one day after receiving Rituxan. Initial evaluation revealed hypoxia and bilateral lung crackles. A CT chest showed new peribronchovascular and centrilobular nodules, concerning for bacterial pneumonia. He was started on IV cefepime and vancomycin, then transitioned to oral levofloxacin after two days of being afebrile. Respiratory viral panel, blood cultures, and CMV testing were negative. His oxygen requirement improved from 2L to 1.5L nasal cannula, and he was discharged home on a 14-day course of levofloxacin, continued immunosuppressants, and a new prescription for esomeprazole for reflux. He was stable at discharge, with plans for outpatient follow-up.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage I through stage IV, or unspecified
